comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 Teaching and Examination Regulations, checked 2026-09-25
comparator.route: General Artificial Intelligence pathway without an optional specialisation
comparator.sourceNotes: For the general 2026–27 pathway, the TER lists 54 EC of compulsory first-year units plus one 6-EC restricted choice (first-listed Information Management); 42 EC of compulsory second-year units plus three 6-EC restricted choices (first-listed Robot Interaction, Data Structures and Algorithms for AI, AI in Health); and 24 EC compulsory third-year project, ethics and research-design units plus one 6-EC restricted choice (first-listed Cognitive Psychology for AI) and 30 EC genuinely open academic minor/profiling space. The zero-credit language test is excluded. This broad coherent 180-EC route has no optional specialisation credential. The TER permits incoming 2026–27 students to opt into Intelligent Systems or Socially Aware Computing under transitional rules, which are not required for this generic target. Every selected restricted choice is one valid unit; other listed options are not combined or presented as mandatory.

alternatives.label: Hybrid intelligence and human cognition
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, machine learning, logic and agent decision making with cognitive science, perception and human behaviour. Ethics and philosophy of mind frame how intelligent systems interact with people; this is a broad AI programme rather than a replica of the VU thesis and project sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum includes extensive technical AI as well as cognition, interaction and ethics; hybrid intelligence describes the actual combination.
progression: Programming and introductory cognition or health studies precede advanced AI, software or health applications. Mathematical Methods precedes higher statistics and neural networks; in the technical route Algorithms and Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms. All formal prerequisites and the fixed 2026–29 term offers were checked.

alternatives.label: AI algorithms and computer systems
alternatives.concept: Emphasises intelligent agents, machine learning and neural networks alongside software development, algorithms, databases, numerical methods and computing infrastructure. Human interaction and ethics remain foundations, but the additional curriculum develops technical computer-science depth.
alternatives.labelReason: The 24 courses devote considerably more space to technical computer science and mathematics than the other programmes.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses replace cognitive science and social psychology with networks, software engineering, advanced algorithms and numerical/multivariable mathematical methods; this is a materially different route into AI system construction.
progression: Programming and introductory cognition or health studies precede advanced AI, software or health applications. Mathematical Methods precedes higher statistics and neural networks; in the technical route Algorithms and Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms. All formal prerequisites and the fixed 2026–29 term offers were checked.

alternatives.label: AI for health, behaviour and care
alternatives.concept: Combines AI, machine learning, vision and robotics with biomedical foundations, epidemiology, physiology and developmental and health psychology. It supports critical study of socially assistive and health-oriented AI while acknowledging that UCR does not offer a clinical AI deployment course.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum links AI systems with substantive biological and behavioural knowledge needed for health applications, without claiming clinical qualification.
alternatives.distinctness: The health route replaces technical computing and some general cognition and philosophy with biomedical foundations, physiology, epidemiology, health psychology and developmental psychology; those courses respond directly to the evidenced health and social-robot applications.

routeSelection.route: General Artificial Intelligence pathway without an optional specialisation
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic bachelor. The adopted 2026–27 TER makes Intelligent Systems and Socially Aware Computing optional, with transitional conditions for entrants; the ordinary curriculum with first-listed permitted constrained choices is a broad valid 180-EC path. No specialisation is chosen for a stronger UCR match.

selection.assessment: Three conceptually distinct, evidenced UCR curricula pass the 24-course and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates: broad hybrid intelligence and cognition, technical AI system construction, and health/behaviour applications. The energy-systems interest is a separate application direction but the approved maximum of three alternatives is already reached; the isolated teaching direction lacks a specific UCR teacher-education sequence.

notes.text: VU requires a structured AI sequence, restricted choices, a 15-EC independent bachelor project and a 30-EC open minor. UCR can assemble substantial AI, data, cognition and ethics study across its open curriculum but does not reproduce each VU AI project or its mandatory individual research project. Health applications at UCR combine domain study with general AI methods rather than a dedicated clinical AI training unit.
